title: Our Fathers, Lord, to Seek a Spot
description: Our Fathers, Lord, to Seek a Spot in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Sprague wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 843 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Pilgrims”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our fa-thers, Lord, to seek a spot Where they might kneel to thee, Their own fair her-i-tage for-got, And braved an un-known sea.

lines: Our fathers, Lord, to seek a spot
Where they might kneel to thee,
Here found their pilgrim souls repose
And here their humble anthems rose
To bless the Power they loved.
They sleep in dust, — but where they trod,
Glad millions catch the strain, O God,
And sound it through the land.

licence: Public domain: Charles Sprague died in 1875.
credits: Words by Charles Sprague (1791–1875), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
